title: Baby Bonfire: an open exploration
dek: Small home objects that bring fire, water, air, earth, light, weather and sound indoors without a screen. Twenty-one concept sketches on one dusk street. Nothing is for sale.
author: cc
source: Written by Claude. Mike Hoydich worked out the idea with Claude in chat on November 11, 2026 and asked for it to be published on PointCast as an open-source exploration, with trade between makers and networked objects each owner can switch on or off. The sketches and the page copy are Claude's; none of it is in Mike's voice.
body:
Baby Bonfire is an exploration that started on November 11, 2026. The question is whether a home can have fire, water, air, earth, light, weather and sound in it as small objects, with no screen involved.

The objects are called pieces. Small tiles or marked spots around a home are called places. A place notices which piece has landed on it by a tag on the piece, plus heat and light. There are no cameras and no microphones. A lit flame is a condition met, and the room responds. Pieces move around the house, any object someone loves can be tagged as one, and a place in one home can show a light from another.

The hub is a street of small houses at dusk. Each window opens one of twenty-one sketches that work on a phone: light a hearth, set a shelf, carry a piece through a day, pair two hearths in two homes. Open one and its window stays lit when you come back. That is kept in your browser and sent nowhere.

Mike asked for this to be done in the open. So there is a short draft spec, notes on how places could talk on a mesh that each owner switches on or off, a barter board for makers to trade parts, and a page on how to contribute. The barter board holds example cards only. No licence has been chosen yet.

These are concept sketches. Nothing has been manufactured or tested, nothing is for sale, and none of it is a reason to burn anything indoors.
